Hi Sarah — great questions, thanks for laying them out so clearly. Quick answers below and I copied Ben (SE) and Marissa (billing) to pull together a short example invoice.

- System messages: counted as input tokens. We meter by the serialized tokenized bytes that hit the model inference path; system + user + assistant (when provided inline) are all part of the input token total.
- Tool outputs: tool responses that are injected back into the model for further decoding are billed as output tokens for the original request. If a tool response is stored separately and then submitted in a subsequent prompt, that later submission is counted as input at that time. We do not invoice tool outputs as a separate "tool" line in the standard hosted ratecard — they appear under output token usage.
- Streaming: billing is based on final tokenization for that request. We do not round per streamed chunk. If a stream is interrupted (connection drop) and the request remains incomplete, we bill only completed tokens as reported by the model runtime for that session.
- Rounding: we round up to the next whole token at the request level. Rounding happens before discounts are applied (i.e., we compute billed tokens for each request -> sum for the period -> apply any committed usage discount bands).
- KV cache: cached KV usage avoids re-computing prefix tokens on the runtime, but you will still see the same billed tokens if the full prompt (including cache expansion) is materialized and sent to the model in that request. We have an optional prefix caching mode that can reduce billed input tokens when you use our SDK hooks; Ben will describe that in his note.

Ben and Marissa — can you attach an example invoice that shows the arithmetic for 1.2B tokens at our hosted baseline rate, then apply a 10% commit? Sarah asked whether discounting happens pre/post rounding; I wrote above that rounding is per-request then discounts apply at the aggregate. Please correct me if I'm off.

Hi Sarah — Ben (SE) here with a compact worked example and one implementation note about streaming/tooling. Quoted your bullets and annotated: 

> Do "system" messages get billed as input tokens?
Yes — everything that contributes to the input token stream that the model processes in a request is counted as input. Example: if you send a 12-token system instruction + 88-token user prompt, that's 100 input tokens.

> When we use tool calling, are tool outputs counted as output tokens or a separate line?
If the tool output is returned by the model as part of the same response generation, it's output tokens on that request. If your pipeline calls a tool and then later includes the tool output as part of a new prompt, that later inclusion becomes input tokens on that subsequent request. We intentionally keep a single token rate line for input and a single line for output on hosted invoices to avoid double-counting confusion.

> If responses stream, is billing based on final token count or per chunk?
Final per-request tokenization is used. For streaming, tokens emitted incrementally are not rounded per chunk. We tally the final token count the runtime reports for the request and apply rounding once at the end of that request.

> Rounding policy?
We round up to the next whole token per request. Example: request tokenization = 124.2 (internal float) -> billed = 125 for that request. Summation across requests yields the monthly billed tokens. Then discounts are applied to the total.

Worked invoice example (short):
- Baseline hosted rates: input = $0.0008 / token, output = $0.0012 / token (see attached PDF for exact bands).
- Assumed split for your workload: 60% input / 40% output on token volume (you can share a sample 24h trace and I can re-run numbers).
- 1.2B combined tokens -> assume 720M input, 480M output after rounding per-request.
- Pre-discount cost = (720,000,000 * 0.0008) + (480,000,000 * 0.0012) = $576,000 + $576,000 = $1,152,000.
- Apply 10% committed usage discount to the aggregate (post-rounding per our current billing flow) -> $1,036,800.

Notes / edge cases:
- If you have many tiny calls (e.g., 1–3 token prompts), per-request rounding can add ~1 token overhead per call. If that pattern dominates, commit bands or batching can meaningfully reduce the effective price/token.
- Prefix caching via our SDK can avoid re-sending large static context; when enabled and used correctly it reduces billed input tokens because the client does not re-serialize the cached prefix into the request. We'll need to enable the feature on your org and update the SDK usage — I can draft an implementation guide.
- For streaming where the client closes early (user cancel), we only bill the tokens the runtime completed.

I'll attach a CSV example with the exact line math (rounded tokens per request aggregated) and a second CSV that applies discount pre-rounding for comparison per Sarah's ask.
